experiment: Proposed 2026-09-18-gap-countries-latam-pacific (PR #27, evaluate 2026-09-22): adds Mexico, Argentina, Philippines and Australia to GAP_COUNTRIES in fetch-news-api.js. Every goal metric is met, so this is not a breach repair — it acts on the one measure moving the wrong way for a third consecutive audit, using the only lever that targets source location rather than source name. Token-neutral: Q3 passes the whole list in one call, so array length does not change per-cycle NewsAPI spend.
weakestArea: Regional concentration, and it is worse than the region tally admits. uniqueRegions fell 6 to 5 with Oceania at zero, but the real figure is in the datelines: 24 of 59 articles are US-datelined (41% of output), so the AM count of 29 is ~83% one country. Latin America contributed three articles (Guayaquil, Santa Elena, Roseaux) and Africa fell 7 to 4. The metric passes because its floor is 4 regions — a threshold that cannot distinguish genuine global spread from a US-plus-four-token-regions day.
watching: Washington and New York alone supply 17 of 59 datelines, the tightest two-city concentration in the recorded window, and San Francisco adds three more on the tech side.
Africa halved from 7 to 4 with Khartoum, Minna, Ogere and Lome the only datelines — Sudan's four-story run noted yesterday did not repeat.
Korea produced two separate Seoul stories plus a Mount Mantap item, an unusually dense Korean-peninsula signal worth checking for a shared underlying event.
Nuuk appears again, and the region ladder reads Greenland as AM — a small but recurring distortion of the Americas count that is geography, not sourcing.
CoinDesk at 5 and Bloomberg at 5 are the joint-second outlets behind Al Jazeera's 8, keeping the crypto/financial-enforcement thread accumulating without an editorial frame for a third day.
coverageGaps: Oceania is entirely absent today after a single article yesterday; Pacific climate, fisheries and regional security remain structurally invisible.
Latin America produced three articles and Mexico produced none, despite being the largest non-US economy in the hemisphere and absent from GAP_COUNTRIES until today.
Southeast Asia appears only through Jakarta, Banten and Kuala Lumpur; the Philippines and Vietnam have no reporting origin in the feed.
Africa's four stories are all West African or Sudanese — no East African, Horn, or Maghreb dateline despite Kenya, Somalia, Morocco and Algeria all sitting in GAP_COUNTRIES.
context: Output held at 59 across 5 completed cycles with freshness near its best (median 0.2, max 1.3), zero duplicates, 45 unique sources and top-outlet share at 14% — every stated goal is met with margin, and sci-tech at 41% is the second-highest in the window. Cycle duration rose again to 1589s from 1427s, driven by the writer (412s avg) rather than the editor (185s), which stays far clear of its 1800s timeout. The standing finding from the two 2026-05 selector-floor experiments is that multi-source rate is capped by feed supply, not selector behaviour, which is why today's experiment targets the upstream feed instead; its most likely failure mode is displacement, since Q3 returns a fixed 100 articles by sourceImportance and Australian and Mexican outlets outrank Somali and Nigerian ones on that sort — hence the explicit Africa and OIC-coverage guardrails.
